overview: This single-page Department of State list-of-papers entry summarizes a report from Japan concerning a proposed reduction in railway freight rates. The measure was intended chiefly to counter declining railway revenues and reduce production costs, with two alternatives under consideration: a general 20 percent cut or a sliding reduction of 10 to 20 percent for materials used in production. The heading also contains an unexplained or possibly misread reference to London.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: Diplomatic official reporting from Japan; specific position not stated in the text

subfiles.title: List-of-papers entry on proposed railway freight-rate reductions in Japan
subfiles.about: An abstract records two proposed schemes for reducing Japanese railway freight rates in response to falling revenues and production costs.
subfiles.summary: The entry reports that reducing freight rates was being considered principally to counter declining railway revenues and to assist the public by lowering the cost of production. Two alternatives are described: a 20 percent reduction and a sliding-scale reduction of 10 to 20 percent on materials used in production. The sheet notes that further details were attached, but those details are not present in the supplied file text.

interest: The item is useful as a compact record of Japanese railway-rate policy during the early phase of the Great Depression, showing that freight reductions were presented both as revenue policy and as economic relief for producers and consumers. Its comparison of a uniform cut with a targeted sliding scale offers evidence of the policy alternatives then being considered. Because only the Department of State abstract survives here, it also illustrates how diplomatic reports were indexed and summarized within the decimal-file system.
